chunks: ʿUqbah ibn Khālid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled with shufʿah between partners in lands and dwellings.
And he said: 'There is no harm and no reciprocating harm.'

key_terms.إِضْرَارَ: causing harm in return or deliberately inflicting harm
key_terms.الشُّرَكَاءِ: co-owners or partners who share ownership in property
key_terms.بِالشُّفْعَةِ: the right of pre-emption granted to a partner before sale to an outsider
key_terms.ضَرَرَ: harm or injury inflicted upon another

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of shufʿah and 'lā ḍarar wa lā iḍrār' mean in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم affirmed the right of shufʿah among co-owners in land and houses. It also includes the foundational legal maxim that harm and reciprocal harming are not permitted, which underlies many rulings concerning rights and transactions.
